title: GitHub Brings Stacked Pull Requests to Public Preview
gist: GitHub launched Stacked Pull Requests in public preview, letting developers break large changes into smaller dependent PRs reviewed and merged independently. The feature explicitly targets the growing mismatch between AI-accelerated code generation and limited human review capacity, framing code review as the primary control point for whether AI improves or degrades software quality.

themes.theme: Review capacity as the new bottleneck

insights.claim: GitHub's Stacked Pull Requests aim to balance the increasing speed of AI-assisted code generation against the limited capacity of human code reviewers, addressing review quality becoming the primary bottleneck as development velocity rises.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Frames tooling investment around review throughput, the binding constraint once AI makes code generation cheap.
insights.quote: As development velocity increases, review quality risks becoming the primary bottleneck in software delivery.
insights.locator: The timing of the announcement paragraph

insights.claim: Stacked pull requests solve the review problem by reducing review scope rather than accelerating review itself, so each PR represents a single logical step like introducing an API or updating a schema that is easier to understand, validate, and less likely to introduce defects.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Smaller-scope reviews are a concrete lever to keep quality high without asking reviewers to work faster.
insights.locator: Stacked pull requests attempt to solve this paragraph

insights.claim: With stacked changes developers can keep building on earlier work while reviewers evaluate each layer independently, reducing large long-lived feature branches that suffer merge conflicts and encouraging incremental architectural improvements associated with lower deployment risk.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Unblocking dependent work improves flow and reduces the risk profile of large feature deliveries.

insights.claim: Stacked development is not new, with Meta popularizing stacked diffs internally and Graphite and Sapling building dedicated tooling, but by building it natively into GitHub, Microsoft removes the operational overhead that previously discouraged adoption while preserving existing branch protection and merge policies.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Native support could mainstream a workflow that until now required third-party tools or manual branch management.

insights.claim: Research on early agentic-coding adoption found that successful integration of increasingly common AI-generated pull requests still depends heavily on human oversight, with most projects relying on a single experienced reviewer to validate agent contributions before merging.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Confirms a human reviewer remains the gatekeeper for agent code, concentrating risk on review capacity.
insights.locator: Recent research reinforces this challenge paragraph

insights.claim: Code review has become the primary control point determining whether AI improves or degrades software quality, so the future of software engineering depends less on generating more code and more on workflows letting humans and AI collaborate safely at scale.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Positions review process, not model output, as the decisive factor in AI's net effect on code quality.
insights.quote: code review has become the primary control point determining whether AI improves or degrades software quality
insights.locator: Other research examining practitioner opinions paragraph
